title: All satisfiable 2D nearest-neighbor template constraints allow repetitive patterns

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All satisfiable 2D nearest-neighbor template constraints allow repetitive patterns

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Of all 4,294,967,296 two-dimensional constraints defined by allowed templates of a cell and its four neighbors, 766,979,044 cannot be satisfied, and every one of the rest can be satisfied by a repetitive pattern, with 171 repetitive patterns sufficing for all.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: among the 3,527,988,252 that remain, it turns out that every single one can be satisfied by a simple repetitive pattern.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Systems Based on Constraints” (from p. 210), p. 213. Scope: two-dimensional two-color constraints on five-cell (von Neumann) neighborhood templates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-16: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The finite universe, counts, and periodicity property provide unambiguous decision criteria. Modern computation can reproduce the exhaustive result, although careful symmetry reduction and verification make it more than a routine small analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-enumerate all two-color von Neumann-neighborhood template sets using symmetry reduction, decide satisfiability, and search periodic fundamental domains. Reproducing the three stated counts confirms the claim; any mismatching rule or count refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The meaning of “171 patterns” must match the source's symmetry conventions.

A full independent enumeration is computationally large.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.98
operationalizability: 0.97

data adequacy: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a finite, fully specified census, so in principle a recomputation decides it, and the 171 patterns are printed and can be checked against individual constraints now. Reproducing the exact unsatisfiable count is a specialist enumeration far past a few weeks, because some constraints only fail on large regions. Existing public material therefore tests pieces of the census rather than the integer as stated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Encode each subset of the 32 five-cell templates as a constraint, test it against the published list of 171 repetitive patterns, and run a backtracking search where none of those patterns fit. Agreement with 766,979,044 unsatisfiable cases and no satisfiable case outside the 171 patterns would confirm the census; one extra pattern or a shifted count would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
There are 2^32 constraints, and some unsatisfiability witnesses are large finite regions.

The 171 patterns let many constraints be checked quickly, but the exact global count needs the full search.

A bug in the numbering or symmetry reduction would move the integer without changing the mathematics.

discriminating power: 0.84
